and yield_from bare; m3 emits parse_int_digit, parse_int_go,

own comment calls it the named-fn discriminator for nested-fn naming;
reading frame.fn_name through an open row handed it a foreign slot, so
nested fns have never been qualified and the qualification path has been
dormant. A defect in its own right, surfaced by the annotation.

One hypothesis died before it was banked: that qualified names collide
with existing symbols. Duplicate-symbol counts are identical between
generations, 514 and 514, so qualification introduced none. One grep over
artifacts already on disk, and the fourth explanation this arc has killed
by measuring instead of reasoning.

The trap's cause remains unmeasured. Why a module whose only change is

probe is cheap because the diff is 39 lines: read those four functions'
call sites against their definitions, since a renamed definition with a
stale caller assembles and fails at the first call, which fits a 0.97s
death better than anything about rows.

The path now has two steps: fix the discriminator's own defect first, then

mentl/75351d8:
Six probes across five pins each indicted a suspect for the compile
floor and cleared it. The aggregate profile finally names the dominator,
and it is not a data structure or a pass — it is a design decision.

On fn main() = 7: wasi_thread_start carries 48.45% inclusive,
branch_bracket 46.80%, and the two list primitives those brackets run —
list_filled_from specialised on Span at 25.59% self, list_set at 23.17%
self — roughly half the run. At the OS level the same fixture creates
433 distinct threads, 20 concurrent at peak against a 10-thread wasmtime
baseline, measured by polling the task table for help, which loads the
identical module and compiles nothing.

The cause reads straight off the artifact. §11 5.2 serialized the
parallel final on 2026-08-07 with judge_window = 1, because the K=8
fan's correctness rested on published schemes being live-var-free and
live cells raced its branches. The window went to 1; the spawn did not.
layer_judge_walk's own comment says every layer branch runs as a real
task, a spawned instance of the whole module, and judge_blocks spawns a
block of judge_window, joins it, and spawns the next. At window 1 that
is one OS thread per layer branch with no parallelism bought.

Why it hid is the method lesson. An earlier --no-children read of a
smaller capture showed a flat profile topping out at 7%, and that was
banked as "there is no hot spot", which then justified calling the cost
diffuse substrate work. The children view aggregated per symbol shows
two functions owning half the run. A flat self profile over
monomorphized twins hides a dominator.

Stamped, not built: at window 1, can the branch be a direct call? The
comment claims the join stream is byte-identical to the sequential walk
by construction, which argues yes, but the spawn also buys branch-local
ledgers, disjoint mint ranges and a read-only intern view. Whether those
are load-bearing at K=1 or inherited from the K=8 design is the question
to answer against the artifact before

mentl/7505ade:
Two changes:

1. L690: hole syntax in the AI-obsolescence-mechanized example updated
   from `= ?` to `= ??` to match substrate (commit f911df1 landed THole
   token; single `?` is no longer recognized).

2. New "## The Hole Is the Gradient's Absence Marker" section inserted
   immediately above "## The Circular Gradient." Crystallizes the
   read-and-write-are-same-coin insight surfaced by Morgan's prompting:

   - Cursor at finished code = read-mode = Mentl's Synth proposes
     alternatives to current selection
   - Cursor at `??` = write-mode = Mentl's Synth proposes from
     constraint space (no incumbent to compete against)
   - Same Synth tentacle, same constraint space, same proof machinery
   - Different surface presentation depending on candidate occupancy

   `??` is the gradient's syntactic absence marker, NOT a TODO marker
   bolted onto the gradient. It IS the developer's primary write-mode
   verb in Inka — the syntactic surface for "synthesize here at
   whatever constraints I've added."

   Per the Circular Gradient: at loose constraints `??` invites many
   candidates; at tight constraints resolves to one inhabitant. Same
   hole; same Mentl; constraint tightness alone determines candidate-
   space size.

   Substrate + visual identity ties:
   - Substrate: lexer recognizes `??` as THole (commit f911df1)
   - Inka Mono renders `??` as octagonal-socket glyph (commit ce7ab37)
   - 8-sided socket ↔ 8 kernel primitives ↔ 8 Mentl tentacles
   - Empty socket waiting to be filled, 8 tentacles' proof-search behind

Why this insight earns crystallization in INSIGHTS: Morgan's prompting
("are read mode and write mode not two sides of the same coin?") forced
re-reading the Circular Gradient (L1192-1226) and recognizing the
discipline collapse — what I had been splitting into two modes is one
mode with two surface presentations. Crystallizing the insight prevents
future drift back into the false dichotomy.

two-top/752cf54:
Two halves of the same feature: tapes as a thing you can trade.

A sim bump used to make old tapes silently vanish from the REPLAYS list
(the scan strict-decoded and dropped mismatches), which reads as data
loss when it is actually the no-migrations law working. Foreign-version
tapes now list dimmed with a SIM v<n> tag and an inert tap — visible on
this very dev box, where a v9 tape surfaced that had been invisible for
weeks. Only tapes whose FORMAT no longer decodes stay hidden; there is
nothing honest to say about bytes we cannot read.

And the trading loop, stated where the tapes are: a match tape is a
~14 KB file and the sim is deterministic, so a friend's tape plays here
exactly as it played there. The REPLAYS screen now prints the folder it
reads and PLAYBOOK documents the swap in both directions. One-tap
sharing from inside the app wants a FileProvider manifest entry that
cargo-apk cannot express today — named follow-up, the folder is the
feature for now.

Also corrects PLAYBOOK's stale arena-picker paragraph (keys 1-3 /
hashed rooms) to the roster + room-name reality.
